## Summary

There is a potential vulnerability in Traefik's BasicAuth middleware. The middleware does not limit the length of the password before it hashes it, and the MD5-crypt hash formats (`$apr1$`, `$1$`) take more CPU time as the password gets longer. An unauthenticated attacker can send requests with passwords up to the entry point `maxHeaderBytes` limit (1 MiB by default) and use a large amount of CPU on each request, which degrades the availability of Traefik. The patched versions reject passwords longer than 1024 bytes.

## Patches

- https://github.com/traefik/traefik/releases/tag/v2.11.62
- https://github.com/traefik/traefik/releases/tag/v3.7.18
- https://github.com/traefik/traefik/releases/tag/v3.8.0-rc.2
